citation: Gaetan Chenevier, The p-adic analytic space of pseudocharacters of a profinite group and pseudorepresentations over arbitrary rings
theorem: Lemma 3.2; Proposition 3.3; Remark 3.5; Proposition 3.7, first alternative (condition F)
statement_used: Continuous full residual determinant functor is represented by a profinite local W(k)-algebra; condition F makes it Noetherian with finite power-series presentation.
hypotheses_checked: Actual groups are profinite and k is finite of characteristic ell.
Global residual representation is the original diagonal sum of pulled-back characters; local applications have degree one.
Global condition F follows from actual finite topological generation and open-subgroup Schreier; local condition F is exactly T.phiV for every open subgroup.
Every IsCO target is a profinite local ring with finite Artin quotients; continuity agrees with original IsCont.
Original O is treated by explicit W(k)-to-O and completed relative power-series quotient in PRG4/PRG6; flatness is not presumed.
No ell>n, absolute irreducibility, trace-only determinant or n! invertibility premise is used; rank zero handled independently.

statement_used: A power-series ring in finitely many variables over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian.
hypotheses_checked: Every base ring is IsCO and hence Noetherian, or the given coefficient DVR.
All variable index sets Unit, Fin D, Fin q times Fin n and finite presentation variables are finite.

statement_used: Completion is exact on finite modules and equals tensor with the completed base.
hypotheses_checked: Base rings are Noetherian; the ideal used is their maximal ideal.
Modules are finite modules, ideals or quotients of finite modules; submodules are finite by Noetherianity.
The bases are complete, so finite modules and their quotients are complete; Krull intersection supplies separation.
